title: Shopping cart and checkout
idea: A shopping cart design keeps one line per product, prices lines through ordered discount rules, and makes an immutable order only when stock covers every line.
points: A `Cart` holds one line per SKU; adding the same product again merges quantities.
Each discount is a `PriceRule` class, applied in fixed order to a running total.
Checkout checks every line's stock first, then takes them all, under one lock.
The `Order` snapshots each line and its price; later changes cannot alter it.

edges.label: add, remove
edges.caption: The customer adds products. A second add of the same SKU merges into one line.

edges.label: subtotal
edges.caption: Each rule sees the cart and the running total, and returns a discount.

edges.label: total
edges.caption: Order matters: a percentage taken after a free item gives a smaller discount.

edges.label: checkout
edges.caption: Inventory checks every line first. One short line fails the whole checkout.

edges.label: all lines taken
edges.caption: Only then is stock reduced, the cart cleared and an `Order` record created.

edges.label: charge
edges.caption: Payment is a strategy behind an interface. If it fails, put the taken stock back.

code.title: Cart and price rules
code.caption: Money is in cents as `long`. Two rules run in order over a running total.

walk.text: `Product` is a value: a SKU and a price in whole cents.
`add` rejects bad quantities and merges repeat adds into one line.
The extension point: a new promotion is a new `PriceRule` class.
Buy 3 get 1: every fourth unit of that SKU is free.
Rules apply in list order; each one sees the total left by the last.

code.title: All-or-nothing checkout
code.caption: Two carts want the last book. The first wins; the second fails and changes nothing.

walk.text: `Line` carries the unit price, and both are records: the order cannot change after checkout.
A cut-down `Cart` of priced lines, with no `Product` or rules, to keep checkout in focus.
Pass one checks every line. A short line throws before any stock moves.
Pass two takes the stock and clears the cart. `synchronized` makes both passes one step.
Ben's checkout fails on BOOK, so his PEN is not taken and his cart is kept.

pitfalls: Store prices as `long` cents or `BigDecimal`; `double` drifts on sums like 0.1 + 0.2.
Check every line's stock before taking any; a mid-way failure leaves a partial order.
Copy the price into the order at checkout; reading the product later shows today's price.

quiz.q: Swap the rules to `PercentOff(10)` then `BuyNGetOne("PEN", 3)`. What is the final total?
quiz.code:
// subtotal 1800, the cart holds 4 PEN at 150
List.of(new PercentOff(10), new BuyNGetOne("PEN", 3))
quiz.why: Ten percent of 1800 is 180, leaving 1620. The free pen still removes its full 150, so 1470. Rule order changes the result.

takeaway: Lines by SKU, ordered price rules, all-or-nothing checkout, immutable order.
